A Bombardier Learjet 60 carrying nine people has crashed in a residential area of Palm Beach County, Florida, after plunging towards the ground in a dramatic nose-down descent on November 1, 2026. The aircraft, came down near Military Trail and 10th Avenue North in Greenacres, approximately six miles from President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate. The jet erupted into a massive fireball upon impact, prompting an emergency response from local authorities. The circumstances surrounding the sudden descent remain unknown.

The aircraft was reportedly flying from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport (AUS) in Texas to North Eleuthera Airport (ELH) in the Bahamas. According to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), nine people were aboard the business jet. Flight-tracking information from FlightRadar24 and videos circulating on social media have provided an initial picture of the aircraft's final moments, although investigators will need to establish what caused the accident.

The aircraft involved was a Learjet 60 registered as N722BD, serial number 60-271. According to preliminary flight-tracking information, the business jet departed Austin at about 15:37 UTC, climbed to a cruising altitude of around 41,000 feet, then continued east toward Florida . It subsequently entered a rapid descent over the West Palm Beach area, with tracking data indicating an exceptionally high descent rate shortly before the aircraft disappeared from radar. The aircraft crashed in Greenacres, in Palm Beach County, at approximately 12:50 local time.

Videos shared online show the aircraft descending at a steep angle before striking the ground and exploding. The impact reportedly left a crater in the roadway and sent thick black smoke into the surrounding area. Palm Beach County authorities closed Military Trail between Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue North while emergency crews responded. The FAA confirmed that nine people were aboard, but initial reporting did not establish the condition of everyone on board or whether anyone was injured on the ground.

The Learjet 60 is a midsize business jet developed by Bombardier's Learjet division as an evolution of the Learjet 55. It first flew in October 1990 and received certification in January 1993, entering service later that year. The aircraft was designed for corporate and private transportation, combining relatively high cruising speeds with the ability to operate on a variety of business aviation routes.

The aircraft is powered by two Pratt & Whitney Canada PW305A turbofan engines mounted on the rear fuselage. Each engine produces approximately 4,600 pounds of thrust, allowing the Learjet 60 to reach a maximum operating altitude of 51,000 feet (15,545 meters). Its swept wings, winglets, and T-tail are characteristic features of the design.

The investigation into the Greenacres accident will be led by the National Transportation Safety Board ( NTSB ), with assistance from the FAA. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy subsequently confirmed via X that all nine people aboard had been killed, although their identities had not immediately been released. Investigators will examine the aircraft's maintenance history, engine performance, flight-control systems, weather conditions and recorded flight data to establish why it entered such a dramatic descent. No cause has yet been established.

The crash also highlights the importance of examining the final flight data rather than drawing conclusions from dramatic footage alone. While preliminary tracking information indicates an extraordinary descent rate, investigators will need to determine whether the aircraft experienced a mechanical failure, loss of control or another emergency. The NTSB's investigation should provide a clearer understanding of the final moments of the Learjet and the circumstances that led to the fatal accident.

经验丰富的国际民航组织飞行员和空中交通管制员英语语言能力讲师以及会议口译员，热衷于促进航空相关业务中的有效沟通。对航空业有深入的了解，包括航空法规、术语和行业特定的通信协议。自 2014 年以来，她一直在欧洲各地的众多航展上工作。作为一名超轻型飞行员，她在业余时间还致力于提高航空运营的安全性和效率。
本文讲述了一个正在发展的故事。请继续与我们联系，因为我们将在可用时添加更多信息。
2026 年 11 月 1 日，一架载有 9 人的庞巴迪里尔 60 型飞机在佛罗里达州棕榈滩县的一个住宅区坠毁，当时飞机以戏剧性的机头朝下坠落到地面。这架飞机在格林埃克斯的军事步道和第十大道北附近坠毁，距离唐纳德·特朗普总统的海湖庄园约六英里。这架喷气式飞机在撞击后喷发出巨大的火球，促使地方当局做出紧急反应。突然下降的情况仍然未知。
据报道，这架飞机从德克萨斯州的奥斯汀-博格斯多姆国际机场（AUS）飞往巴哈马的北伊柳塞拉机场（ELH）。据美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）称，这架公务机上共有九人。来自 FlightRadar24 的航班跟踪信息和社交媒体上流传的视频提供了飞机最后时刻的初步画面，不过调查人员需要确定事故原因。
涉案飞机是一架 Learjet 60，注册号为 N722BD，序列号为 60-271。根据初步的航班跟踪信息，这架公务机于世界标准时间 15:37 左右从奥斯汀起飞，爬升至约 41,000 英尺的巡航高度，然后继续向东飞往佛罗里达州。随后，它在西棕榈滩地区上空快速下降，跟踪数据显示，在飞机从雷达上消失之前不久，下降率异常高。飞机于当地时间12点50分左右在棕榈滩县格林埃克斯坠毁。

网上分享的视频显示，飞机以大角度下降，然后撞击地面并爆炸。据报道，撞击在道路上留下了一个弹坑，并向周围地区喷出了浓浓的黑烟。棕榈滩县当局关闭了克雷斯特哈文大道 (Cresthaven Boulevard) 和第十大道北 (10th Avenue North) 之间的军事步道，同时紧急救援人员做出了反应。美国联邦航空局确认机上有九人，但初步报告并未确定机上所有人的状况，也没有确定地面上是否有人受伤。
Learjet 60 是庞巴迪 Learjet 部门开发的一款中型公务机，是 Learjet 55 的升级版。它于 1990 年 10 月首飞，并于 1993 年 1 月获得认证，同年晚些时候投入使用。该飞机专为企业和私人运输而设计，结合了相对较高的巡航速度和在各种公务航空航线上运营的能力。
该飞机由安装在机身后部的两台加拿大普惠公司 PW305A 涡轮风扇发动机提供动力。每台发动机可产生约 4,600 磅的推力，使里尔 60 能够达到 51,000 英尺（15,545 米）的最大运行高度。其后掠翼、小翼和 T 型尾翼是该设计的典型特征。
对格林埃克斯事故的调查将由国家运输安全委员会（NTSB）领导，并得到美国联邦航空局（FAA）的协助。交通部长肖恩·达菲随后通过 X 证实，机上九人全部遇难，但他们的身份尚未立即公布。调查人员将检查飞机的维护历史、发动机性能、飞行控制系统、天气状况和记录的飞行数据，以确定飞机为何出现如此剧烈的下降。原因尚未确定。
这次事故还凸显了检查最终飞行数据的重要性，而不是仅从戏剧性的镜头中得出结论。虽然初步跟踪信息显示飞机下降率异常高，但调查人员需要确定飞机是否经历了机械故障、失控或其他紧急情况。美国国家运输安全委员会的调查应该可以更清楚地了解里尔喷气式飞机的最后时刻以及导致致命事故的情况。

A Lufthansa crew member has died in a suspected electrocution accident at a hotel swimming pool in Bengaluru, India. The incident occurred on Friday, 30 October, during a layover at the five-star Conrad Bengaluru hotel.

The victim was identified in Indian media reports as Alexander Maximilian Theiss, a 57-year-old German national working for Lufthansa. He reportedly died alongside a second foreign national, identified as 45-year-old Slovak project manager Juraj Horvat. Both men were swimming in the hotel’s third-floor pool when they apparently suffered electric shocks.
Two other people, an American hotel guest and an Indian pool attendant, were also injured while attempting to rescue the victims. They were taken to hospital and were reportedly out of danger.

Investigators are examining whether faulty underwater pool lighting or electrical installations may have caused electricity to enter the water. However, the exact cause of the incident has not yet been established, and police are investigating possible negligence. The swimming pool was subsequently closed.

Lufthansa confirmed the death of one of its crew members during a layover in Bengaluru, expressing its deep sadness and condolences to the family, friends and colleagues of the deceased. The airline declined to provide further personal details out of respect for the family’s privacy.

summary: The planemaker championing a technological revolution for general aviation everywhere.

body_en: Cirrus Built The SR22 With A Whole-Airplane Parachute & Now It Is The Best-Selling Piston Single Of The Century

Luke Diaz is a freelance military writer with experience with active duty experience in the US Navy as well as defense and industrial engineering. He is a former Naval Flight Officer who performed tactical air control on the carrier-based E-2 Hawkeye.

Cirrus has revolutionized the world of general aviation in the 21st century with its SR22 series single-engine propeller planes, but the game-changing design choice was not due to performance or cost, but rather safety. The SR22 became the leading single-engine piston aircraft of the modern era by shifting industry focus from mechanics to pilot and passenger peace of mind. Cirrus completely upended the GA market with a modern, high-performance plane built entirely around an unprecedented safety mechanism: a whole-airplane parachute.

The crown jewel of the SR20 family is the Cirrus Airframe Parachute System (CAPS), but it is far from the only innovative technology packed inside the lightweight, composite monoplane. Before the SR22 arrived in 2001, the light aircraft market was dominated by legacy, decades-old aluminum designs from manufacturers like Cessna and Piper. The SR22 is built from sleek, rivet-free fiberglass and carbon fiber composites rather than aluminum sheets, allowing for superior aerodynamics, higher speeds, and an incredibly strong cabin fuselage.

The SR22 wings also feature a unique, NASA-designed discontinuous 'cuffed' leading edge. This advanced design makes the outer edges of the wing highly resistant to stalling, drastically minimizing the risk of a fatal spin occurring in critical phases of flight. The planes also feature the safe return emergency Auto Land system developed in collaboration with Garmin Avionics. All of this combined has launched the SR22 to the top sales spot every single year since 2003 and pushed Cirrus' market share to over 50% of global single-engine piston planes.
Metrics That Matter: Why Peace of Mind Beats Pure Performance

While the Cirrus SR22 is the best-selling cross-country machine for 24 consecutive years, it does not hold the crown for absolute top performance metrics like pure speed, payload capacity, or short-field flexibility. If speed is your only metric, the Mooney Acclaim Ultra completely outperforms the Cirrus. Meanwhile, the Cessna 182 Skylane is more rugged, and the Piper Archer is favored by flight schools for efficiency.

Despite the performance disadvantage, Cirrus routinely sells 10 to 15 times more aircraft per year than its direct performance competitors. According to General Aviation News, the Turbocharged SR22T topped the list of piston singles with twice as many sales as the Cessna Skyhawk and the Piper Archer in 2025. As of early 2026, Cirrus has delivered over 8,700 individual SR22 and SR22T aircraft since its debut, and over 11,000 total SR-series planes.

Other aircraft have been around much longer, so their historical lifetime production totals look larger, but their modern appeal has cratered in comparison. Cirrus delivered 691 planes in 2025, with the SR22 and turbocharged SR22T making up 70-80% of the total. While Cessna sells hundreds of 172s, only 40-60 182 Skylanes have been sold this year. Meanwhile, Beechcraft has handed over just about a dozen of its top-of-the-line Bonanza G36s in 2026.
The 'Gimmick' That Won: Facing Down Flight Line Skepticism

Founders Alan and Dale Klapmeier had a personal reason to care about safety when they designed the piston single that catapulted them to the top of the class. According to the Smithsonian, Alan barely survived a midair collision in 1985 and vowed to put a parachute into every future Cirrus. Cirrus now sells more airplanes than any other general aviation builder, but its initial reception was lukewarm.

Cirrus pitched a different kind of airplane when the SR20 arrived in 1999. It came with a composite airframe, a side-mounted yoke, and the famed parachute. The very feature that makes it famous today, CAPS, was initially mocked as a dangerous marketing gimmick. Critics argued that a parachute was an admission of a flawed aerodynamic design. Veteran pilots openly mocked it, claiming it was a 'crutch.'

For the 2001 model year, Cirrus announced the SR22. Cirrus kept fixed landing gear for safety, which many performance purists dismissed as inefficient compared to a Mooney or Bonanza. The SR22 abandoned the traditional heavy center yoke for a side-mounted flight stick, which veteran GA flyers dubbed 'plasticky,' like a video game controller. However, the real headwinds came when amateur pilots began to fall victim to a false sense of security.

The initial skepticism turned into a full-blown safety crisis in the mid-2000s. Inexperienced pilots began flying into severe weather, heavy icing, and thunderstorms that they were not qualified to handle. Shockingly, in many early fatal crashes, pilots never pulled the parachute handle. By 2011, the SR22’s fatal accident rate spiked to 1.6 per 100,000 flight hours, significantly worse than the overall general aviation average of 1.2 at the time.
Rewiring GA Safety Of Flight: From False Security To Gold Standard

Faced with a brand-destroying safety crisis, Cirrus Aircraft and the Cirrus Owners and Pilots Association (COPA) fundamentally changed emergency training. They institutionalized the rule: if you lose control, lose an engine over rough terrain, or experience spatial disorientation in the clouds, pull the handle immediately. The cultural shift worked. By 2014, the SR22's fatal accident rate dropped to 0.42, making it one of the safest single-engine planes in the world.

The company advises pilots to deploy at or above 2,000 feet (610 meters) above the ground, and AOPA relays its advice to “pull early and pull often.” CAPS is a ballistic parachute attached to the airframe that launches via a small rocket. The cabin's red handle overhead releases it, the canopy opens, and the entire airplane descends slowly to the ground.

AOPA says Cirrus fitted parachutes to all of its aircraft starting in 1998 and that it was the first parachute produced in an FAA-certified airplane. More than two decades later, AOPA adds, Cirrus remains the only company that includes a whole airframe parachute as standard equipment on every certified model it sells. Once the safety record matched the marketing hype, the SR22 became unstoppable.

By successfully transforming a 'dangerous luxury toy' reputation into the gold standard of modern aviation safety, the SR22 completely wiped out its competition. Pilot spouses and families strongly prefer Cirrus over Cessnas or Pipers because they know they can pull the red handle if the pilot becomes incapacitated. Cirrus leaned in, continuously updating the plane with the first-ever full glass cockpit in a light piston plane in 2003 and eventually, the Safe Return Autoland button.
body_zh: Cirrus 打造了带有全飞机降落伞的 SR22，现在它是本世纪最畅销的活塞单机
卢克·迪亚兹 (Luke Diaz) 是一位自由军事作家，拥有在美国海军以及国防和工业工程领域服役的现役经验。他是一名前海军飞行军官，曾在舰载 E-2 鹰眼上执行战术空中控制。
西锐凭借其SR22系列单引擎螺旋桨飞机彻底改变了21世纪的通用航空世界，但改变游戏规则的设计选择并不是出于性能或成本，而是出于安全性。通过将行业焦点从机械师转移到让飞行员和乘客安心，SR22 成为现代领先的单引擎活塞飞机。西锐凭借一种完全围绕前所未有的安全机制构建的现代化高性能飞机彻底颠覆了通用航空市场：全飞机降落伞。
SR20 系列皇冠上的明珠是西锐机身降落伞系统 (CAPS)，但它远非这款轻型复合材料单翼飞机所采用的唯一创新技术。在 SR22 于 2001 年问世之前，轻型飞机市场主要由 Cessna 和 Piper 等制造商的已有数十年历史的传统铝制设计主导。 SR22 采用时尚、无铆钉的玻璃纤维和碳纤维复合材料而不是铝板制成，具有卓越的空气动力学性能、更高的速度和极其坚固的机舱机身。
SR22 机翼还具有 NASA 设计的独特的不连续“翻边”前缘。这种先进的设计使机翼的外缘具有很强的抗失速能力，从而大大降低了在飞行关键阶段发生致命旋转的风险。这些飞机还配备了与 Garmin Avionics 合作开发的安全返航紧急自动着陆系统。所有这些加在一起，使 SR22 自 2003 年以来每年都稳居销量榜首，并将西锐的市场份额推至全球单引擎活塞飞机的 50% 以上。
重要的指标：为什么安心胜过纯粹的表现
虽然 Cirrus SR22 连续 24 年成为最畅销的越野机器，但它并未在纯速度、有效负载能力或短场灵活性等绝对顶级性能指标上保持桂冠。如果速度是您唯一的衡量标准，Mooney Acclaim Ultra 的性能完全优于 Cirrus。与此同时，Cessna 182 Skylane 更加坚固，而 Piper Archer 则因效率而受到飞行学校的青睐。
尽管存在性能劣势，西锐每年的飞机销量通常是其直接性能竞争对手的 10 至 15 倍。据《通用航空新闻》报道，涡轮增压 SR22T 荣登活塞单机排行榜榜首，其 2025 年销量是 Cessna Skyhawk 和 Piper Archer 的两倍。截至 2026 年初，西锐自首次亮相以来已交付超过 8,700 架 SR22 和 SR22T 飞机，SR 系列飞机总数超过 11,000 架。

其他飞机的历史时间要长得多，因此它们的历史寿命总产量看起来更大，但相比之下，它们的现代吸引力却大打折扣。西锐在 2025 年交付了 691 架飞机，其中 SR22 和涡轮增压 SR22T 占总数的 70-80%。虽然塞斯纳销售了数百架 172，但今年仅售出了 40-60 60 60 182 Skylanes。与此同时，Beechcraft 已于 2026 年交付了大约十几架顶级 Bonanza G36。
获胜的“噱头”：直面航线怀疑论
创始人艾伦·克拉普梅尔 (Alan Klapmeier) 和戴尔·克拉普梅尔 (Dale Klapmeier) 在设计活塞单缸发动机时出于个人原因关心安全性，并使其跻身同类产品之列。据史密森学会报道，艾伦在 1985 年的一次空中相撞事故中险些生还，并发誓要为未来的每一架西锐飞机安装降落伞。西锐现在销售的飞机比任何其他通用航空制造商都多，但最初的反响却冷淡。
当 SR20 于 1999 年问世时，西锐推出了一款不同类型的飞机。它配备了复合材料机身、侧装操纵杆和著名的降落伞。使其如今闻名的功能 CAPS 最初被嘲笑为一种危险的营销噱头。批评者认为降落伞是对空气动力学设计缺陷的承认。经验丰富的飞行员公开嘲笑它，声称它是“拐杖”。
对于 2001 年车型，西锐 (Cirrus) 发布了 SR22。为了安全起见，西锐保留了固定起落架，许多性能纯粹主义者认为与穆尼或博南扎相比效率低下。 SR22 放弃了传统的重型中心操纵杆，采用侧装飞行杆，资深 GA 飞行员将其称为“塑料”，就像视频游戏控制器一样。然而，当业余飞行员开始成为错误的安全感的受害者时，真正的阻力就来了。
最初的怀疑在 2000 年代中期演变成一场全面的安全危机。缺乏经验的飞行员开始在他们没有资格应对的恶劣天气、严重结冰和雷暴天气中飞行。令人震惊的是，在许多早期的致命事故中，飞行员从未拉动降落伞手柄。到2011年，SR22的致命事故率飙升至每10万飞行小时1.6起，明显低于当时通用航空整体平均1.2起。
重新审视 GA 的飞行安全：从虚假安全到黄金标准
面对品牌毁灭性的安全危机，西锐飞机公司和西锐所有者和飞行员协会 (COPA) 从根本上改变了应急培训。他们将规则制度化：如果你失去控制，在崎岖的地形上失去引擎，或者在云中经历空间迷失方向，请立即拉动手柄。文化转变起了作用。到2014年，SR22的致命事故率下降至0.42，使其成为世界上最安全的单引擎飞机之一。
该公司建议飞行员部署在距地面 2,000 英尺（610 米）或以上的高度，AOPA 转达了“早拉、经常拉”的建议。 CAPS 是一种附在机身上的弹道降落伞，通过小型火箭发射。机舱头顶上的红色手柄将其释放，座舱盖打开，整个飞机缓慢下降到地面。
AOPA 表示，西锐从 1998 年开始在其所有飞机上安装降落伞，这是第一款在 FAA 认证的飞机上生产的降落伞。 AOPA 补充道，二十多年后，西锐仍然是唯一一家将整个机身降落伞作为其销售的每款认证型号的标准装备的公司。一旦安全记录与营销宣传相匹配，SR22 就变得势不可挡。
SR22 成功地将“危险的豪华玩具”的声誉转变为现代航空安全的黄金标准，彻底消灭了竞争对手。与塞斯纳斯或派珀相比，飞行员配偶和家人更喜欢西锐，因为他们知道，如果飞行员丧失工作能力，他们可以拉动红色手柄。 2003 年，西锐不断投入精力，不断更新飞机，在轻型活塞飞机上推出了首个全玻璃驾驶舱，并最终推出了安全返回自动着陆按钮。

title_en: Why The Flagship Of The World’s Elite Airlines Is No Longer In Production
title_zh: 为什么世界精英航空​​公司的旗舰不再生产
summary: Boeing recently made the decision to halt the production of one of its best-selling widebody aircraft.
summary_zh: 波音公司最近决定停止生产其最畅销的宽体飞机之一。
body_en: The leading independent voice for aviation news and insight.

In 2004, the airline sector was revolutionized by the Boeing 777-300ER (extended range) variant of the 777 family. It was first flown commercially by Air France, and at the time, Boeing claimed it was "the most technologically advanced airplane in the industry" , surpassing previous 777-200 and 777-200ER variants, and raising the bar in terms of comfort and range.

The 777-300ER featured updated systems, and at the time, it was equipped with the most powerful commercial jet engine available, the General Electric GE90-115B turbofan. Thanks to its long range and excellent fuel efficiency, the 777-300ER became extremely popular for long-haul routes, maximizing profits through operational efficiency and high capacity.

It remains a popular aircraft among airline fleets worldwide, including at China Eastern Airlines, which used it to launch the world's longest direct one-stop flight , according to Islands. As Boeing begins moving into the era of the 777X, this article takes a look at the 777-300ER, following the last example rolling off the production line.

According to Aerospace Global News, only a single Boeing 777-300ER was produced in 2024 . This final example of the variant was delivered in December to Altavair LP. Altavair is an aircraft finance company, an aircraft lessor and management company, which specializes in acquiring, leasing, repurposing, and selling commercial jet aircraft and engines.

Since its creation in 2003, Altavair has completed over $12 billion in commercial aircraft lease transactions and represents over 300 Boeing and Airbus jets. The production of the final 777-300ER ends a nearly two-decade production run of the world’s best-selling widebody aircraft. It also marked the end of a significant era of commercial aviation history.

According to Boeing, 833 examples of the 777-300ER were delivered , making up a huge portion of the 1,781 examples of the 777 family delivered and 2,457 ordered. These figures make the 777-300ER the most popular variant of the 777, which is the best-selling widebody airliner family in history.

Boeing had gradually slowed the production of the 777-300ER in favor of testing and refining the 777X. Before the last aircraft was delivered to Altavair, the last time a 777-300ER was delivered was in 2022, when only three were delivered to Thai Airways , according to Air Data News.

Altavair's 2024 777-300ER had previously been on order by China Southern Airlines, but with COVID slowdowns, the order fell through, and the aircraft was stored for nearly five years. As such, when Altavair leased the aircraft to Ethiopian Airlines in 2024, it still bore China Southern livery.

Previously, there were five additional 777-300ERs on order with Pakistan International Airlines, and these brought the total number of orders up to 838. However, as of May 2025, the order had been outstanding for 13 years, and according to multiple publications in September, the delivery of the Altavair 777-300ER officially became the last to be delivered, ending production of the type for good.

The 777-300ER was introduced in 2004, and compared to other 777 variants that existed at the time, it was revolutionary. The variant was suited for long-haul air travel, with an impressive 7,370 nautical miles of range. This was achieved thanks to the twin-engined 777-300ER's efficient design.

However, it was also because the General Electric GE90 high-bypass turbofan engines it was equipped with were the most powerful commercial jet engines in the world. In terms of power, the GE90 produced 115,300 pounds of thrust. The engine was first used with the 777-300ER, and later with the 777-200LR Worldliner (first delivered in 2006), and then the 777F freighter variant, which was based on the 777-200LR and first delivered in 2009.

Boeing's 777-200LR would be the world's longest-range in-service commercial aircraft in the world, until it was surpassed by the Airbus A350-900ULR, which still holds the title today after entering service with Singapore Airlines in September 2018. The power of the GE90 was finally surpassed by the General Electric GE9X in July 2019, according to Guinness World Records.

GE Aerospace's GE9X is due to enter service with the delivery of the first 777X. The engine produces 134,300 pounds of thrust, making it the most powerful commercial aircraft engine ever built, but also the largest, due to its fan diameter of 11.2 feet. Its construction also incorporates composite carbon-fiber materials, allowing it to achieve up to 10% greater fuel efficiency compared to the GE90-115B, according to General Electric.

While the power of the GE90 engine has its own charm for horsepower enthusiasts, there were other factors that made the 777-300ER popular with airlines. The aspects detailed in the table below, which every airline desires in a commercial jetliner, were key catalysts behind its success.

The fuselage of the 777-300 variant, and the long-range 777-300ER, is stretched, being a little over 33 feet longer than the 777-200. Thanks to its stretched fuselage, the 777-300ER can carry a large number of passengers, typically 365 in a three-class configuration, and 396 in a two-class configuration. This made it ideal for dense long-haul trunk routes and high-demand international sectors.

The 'ER' designation stood for Extended Range, and the 777-300ER offered a significant range improvement over the baseline 777-300. For airlines, this increased range meant that non-stop long-haul flights that previously required larger or less efficient aircraft became much more commercially viable.

The 777-300ER's high-bypass turbofans and modern systems, combined with its light twin-engined design, produced lower fuel burn per seat than many older widebodies, particularly quadjets, that might otherwise be used to operate dense routes. Thus, airlines could offer more direct long routes at attractive costs to customers, increasing earnings potential and passenger convenience.
body_zh: 航空新闻和见解的领先独立声音。
2004 年，777 系列的波音 777-300ER（增程型）变体彻底改变了航空业。它首先由法国航空进行商业飞行，当时波音公司声称它是“业内技术最先进的飞机”，超越了之前的 777-200 和 777-200ER 型号，并在舒适度和航程方面提高了标准。
777-300ER 采用更新的系统，并配备了当时最强大的商用喷气发动机：通用电气 GE90-115B 涡轮风扇发动机。凭借其远航程和出色的燃油效率，777-300ER 在长途航线上非常受欢迎，通过运营效率和高运力实现利润最大化。
据Islands称，它仍然是全球航空公司机队中最受欢迎的飞机，其中包括中国东方航空，该公司利用它推出了世界上最长的直飞航班。随着波音开始进入 777X 时代，本文将继最后一架下线的 777-300ER 飞机之后，来介绍一下 777-300ER。
据《航空航天全球新闻》报道，2024 年仅生产了一架波音 777-300ER。该变体的最后一个示例已于 12 月交付给 Altavair LP。 Altavair 是一家飞机金融公司、飞机租赁和管理公司，专门从事收购、租赁、重新利用和销售商用喷气式飞机和发动机。
选择一架飞机，看看现在有多少架飞机在空中
自 2003 年成立以来，Altavair 已完成超过 120 亿美元的商用飞机租赁交易，代理超过 300 架波音和空客喷气式飞机。最终 777-300ER 的生产结束了全球最畅销宽体飞机近两年的生产历程。这也标志着商业航空历史上一个重要时代的结束。
据波音称，777-300ER 已交付 833 架，占 777 系列交付的 1,781 架和订购的 2,457 架的很大一部分。这些数字使 777-300ER 成为 777 最受欢迎的变体，777 是历史上最畅销的宽体客机系列。
波音公司逐渐放慢了 777-300ER 的生产，转而测试和改进 777X。据《航空数据新闻》报道，在最后一架飞机交付给 Altavair 之前，上一次交付 777-300ER 是在 2022 年，当时泰国航空只交付了三架。
Altavair 的 2024 款 777-300ER 此前曾被中国南方航空订购，但随着新冠疫情放缓，订单流产，飞机被存放了近五年。因此，当 Altavair 在 2024 年将这架飞机租赁给埃塞俄比亚航空公司时，它仍然带有中国南方航空的标志。
此前，巴基斯坦国际航空公司还额外订购了五架777-300ER，这使得订单总数达到838架。然而，截至2025年5月，该订单已经悬而未决13年，根据多份出版物，9月份Altavair 777-300ER的交付正式成为最后交付的飞机，永远结束了该机型的生产。
777-300ER 于 2004 年推出，与当时存在的其他 777 型号相比，它具有革命性。该型号适合长途航空旅行，航程高达 7,370 海里。这得益于双引擎 777-300ER 的高效设计。
不过，也是因为它所配备的通用电气GE90高涵道比涡扇发动机是世界上最强大的商用喷气发动机。在动力方面，GE90 产生了 115,300 磅的推力。该发动机首先用于 777-300ER，后来用于 777-200LR Worldliner（于 2006 年首次交付），然后是基于 777-200LR 的 777F 货机变体，于 2009 年首次交付。
波音 777-200LR 曾是全球在役航程最远的商用飞机，直到被空中客车 A350-900ULR 超越，而空客 A350-900ULR 于 2018 年 9 月开始与新加坡航空合作后至今仍保持着这一称号。根据吉尼斯世界纪录，GE90 的动力最终于 2019 年 7 月被通用电气 GE9X 超越。
GE 航空航天公司的 GE9X 预计将随着第一架 777X 的交付而投入使用。该发动机可产生 134,300 磅的推力，使其成为有史以来最强大的商用飞机发动机，同时也是最大的，因为其风扇直径为 11.2 英尺。据通用电气称，其结构还采用了复合碳纤维材料，与 GE90-115B 相比，燃油效率提高了 10%。
虽然 GE90 发动机的动力对于马力爱好者来说有其自身的魅力，但还有其他因素使 777-300ER 受到航空公司的欢迎。下表详述的各个方面是每家航空公司都希望商用喷气式飞机能够实现的，也是其成功背后的关键催化剂。
777-300 变型和远程 777-300ER 的机身被拉伸，比 777-200 长 33 英尺多一点。由于机身加长，777-300ER 可以承载大量乘客，通常三舱配置可承载 365 名乘客，两舱配置可承载 396 名乘客。这使其成为密集长途干线和高需求国际航线的理想选择。
“ER”名称代表扩展航程，777-300ER 比基准 777-300 的航程有了显着改进。对于航空公司而言，航程的增加意味着以前需要更大或效率较低的飞机的直达长途航班变得更具商业可行性。
777-300ER 的高涵道比涡轮风扇发动机和现代系统与其轻型双引擎设计相结合，与许多老式宽体飞机（特别是四喷气发动机）相比，每个座位的燃油消耗更低，否则这些飞机可能用于运营密集的航线。因此，航空公司可以以对客户有吸引力的成本提供更直接的长途航线，从而增加盈利潜力和乘客便利性。

title_en: The Untold Truth Of How Airlines Use Basic Economy To Really Upsell Passengers
title_zh: 航空公司如何利用基础经济舱来真正向乘客推销产品的不为人知的真相
summary: Restrictive low-cost fares attract travelers before airlines use rising upgrade prices and reduced loyalty benefits to make passengers pay more.
summary_zh: 在航空公司利用上涨的升舱价格和减少忠诚度福利来让乘客支付更多费用之前，限制性的低成本票价吸引了旅客。
body_en: The Untold Truth Of How Airlines Use Basic Economy To Really Upsell Passengers

Jack comes to Simple Flying with a lifelong interest in all things aviation. He holds a degree in Aerospace Engineering from Georgia Tech, and is a certified private and remote pilot. Beyond these experiences, Jack previously worked for a corporate flight department where he gained first-hand experience in the world of business aviation. Currently, Jack works in the professional services industry and continues to build his flight hours outside of work.

Basic Economy is presented as the cheapest way to fly, but its commercial purpose extends beyond offering a lower fare. Major US airlines use the restricted ticket as an entry point in a tiered pricing system, then encourage customers to pay more for seat selection, flexibility, loyalty programs , and other benefits that standard economy once included. The result is a fare that can look attractive in search results while making the next option appear increasingly necessary by the time a traveler reaches checkout.

The strategy has become more effective as the gap between basic and standard economy has widened. Thrifty Traveler found that avoiding basic economy commonly costs at least $100 extra roundtrip on domestic routes and roughly $240 on transatlantic trips. Airlines have also tightened mileage, seating, and upgrade rules, using the low headline price to attract shoppers before steering many toward higher-revenue fares.
A Low Headline Fare Creates The First Step In The Sales Funnel

Delta Air Lines introduced basic economy in 2012, with other major US airlines following from 2013 as they responded to the growth of ultra-low-cost competitors such as Spirit and Frontier. Those carriers advertised low base fares and charged separately for services traditional airlines had generally included. Basic economy lets network airlines display competitive prices without discounting every standard economy seat.

The design divided customers by willingness to pay for convenience and flexibility. Someone focused on reaching a destination could accept the restrictions, while a traveler who wanted advance seat selection, a carry-on allowance, or the ability to change plans could choose a more expensive product. American Airlines President at the time, Robert Isom, summarized the commercial logic in comments to CNBC : “ Basic economy is not a price cut .” The fare created a lower price point, but it also allowed the airline to charge more for the standard product. Rather than discounting the existing economy ticket, carriers removed selected benefits from it and placed those benefits behind a higher fare.

Basic economy also anchors the price comparison. A low advertised fare attracts attention in search results; the booking page then displays its limitations beside the cost of avoiding them. A shopper may decide the difference is acceptable once the consequences become clear. The entry price has done its job even if the airline would prefer the customer to buy up.
The Buy-Up Rate Matters More Than Basic Economy Sales

Airlines can judge the success of basic economy by how many customers move to a higher fare, not simply by the number who purchase the cheapest ticket. American said approximately 60% of passengers who looked at its basic economy option paid to move up to standard economy. The proportion was higher at United Airlines , whose restrictions have historically been among the industry's toughest. United executives previously said only 16% of domestic passengers actually purchased basic economy.

The figures explain why airlines keep a fare they do not necessarily want most customers to buy. Basic economy serves as a reference price, while standard economy captures travelers who decide the savings do not justify the restrictions. The low fare also remains available to attract shoppers who might otherwise choose a competitor. The booking interface makes the comparison immediate: omitted benefits appear alongside the next tier's price. Passengers weigh specific inconveniences against the cost of avoiding them. A family concerned about sitting together, for example, may view the higher fare as a practical necessity rather than an optional upgrade.

Passengers effectively sort themselves: those who accept a middle seat and strict conditions choose the lower fare, while those who value predictability pay more. Nearly identical seats can therefore generate different revenue. The figures should not be treated as a current, like-for-like conversion rate across both airlines. They come from different disclosures and periods, and United's 16% figure described the share of domestic passengers who bought basic economy, not the proportion of shoppers who upgraded. Still, the contrast illustrates why a carrier can sell relatively few basic tickets while benefiting from the product's presence in the fare display. The cheapest option helps establish the market's entry price; the more important commercial outcome is the revenue earned across the full range of fare choices.

The financial gap between basic and standard economy has grown substantially. Thrifty Traveler's October 2026 review found that Alaska, American, Delta, JetBlue, and United commonly charge at least $100 more roundtrip for standard economy on domestic flights. Some comparisons approach or exceed $150, particularly on Delta. The additional cost is no longer limited to long journeys or peak travel periods; it can appear on relatively short domestic routes.

On transatlantic itineraries, the difference has risen from roughly $150 roundtrip a few years ago to about $240 today. Some routes cost more, such as a Los Angeles-to-Tokyo example where Delta priced standard economy hundreds of dollars above Main Basic. These are fare comparisons, not fixed fees. The gap varies with route, date, demand, and remaining inventory as revenue-management systems adjust prices. A $100 difference on one itinerary is not a universal surcharge, but the broader pattern shows that restoring standard economy benefits has become more expensive.
Airlines Are Removing Loyalty Benefits To Make The Upgrade More Attractive

The restrictions now reach beyond the flight itself. Airlines have reduced rewards on their lowest fares, making basic economy less valuable to frequent flyers and status seekers. United changed MileagePlus earning for basic economy tickets issued on or after April 2, 2026. General members without Premier status or an eligible United credit card no longer earn redeemable miles on those fares, while qualifying elites and cardholders still earn reduced miles. The change was part of a broader loyalty overhaul that gives customers with United co-branded cards more favorable earning rates and award-flight benefits. Reuters described the move as an effort to encourage credit-card adoption and deepen loyalty to the airline. Reuters and The Points Guy outlined the changes.
body_zh: 航空公司如何利用基础经济舱来真正向乘客推销产品的不为人知的真相
Jack 带着对航空一切事物的终生兴趣加入了 Simple Flying。他拥有佐治亚理工学院的航空航天工程学位，并且是一名经过认证的私人和远程飞行员。除了这些经验之外，杰克还曾在公司飞行部门工作过，在那里他获得了公务航空领域的第一手经验。目前，杰克在专业服务行业工作，并在工作之外继续增加飞行时间。
基础经济舱被认为是最便宜的飞行方式，但其商业目的不仅仅是提供较低的票价。美国主要航空公司将限制机票作为分级定价系统的切入点，然后鼓励客户为座位选择、灵活性、忠诚度计划以及标准经济舱曾经包含的其他福利支付更多费用。其结果是，票价在搜索结果中看起来很有吸引力，同时在旅行者结账时使下一个选项显得越来越必要。
随着基础经济和标准经济之间差距的拉大，这一战略变得更加有效。 Thrifty Traveler 发现，如果不选择基本经济舱，国内航线的往返费用通常至少要多花 100 美元，而跨大西洋航线的往返费用则要多花大约 240 美元。航空公司还收紧了里程、座位和升舱规则，利用较低的总体价格来吸引购物者，然后引导许多人转向更高收入的票价。
低标题价格创造了销售漏斗的第一步
达美航空于 2012 年推出了基础经济舱，美国其他主要航空公司也从 2013 年开始跟进，以应对 Spirit 和 Frontier 等超低成本竞争对手的增长。这些航空公司宣传低基本票价，并对传统航空公司通常包含的服务单独收费。基础经济舱让网络航空公司能够展示具有竞争力的价格，而无需为每个标准经济舱座位打折。

该设计根据是否愿意为便利性和灵活性付费来划分客户。专注于到达目的地的旅客可以接受这些限制，而想要提前选择座位、随身携带行李或更改计划的旅客则可以选择更昂贵的产品。美国航空时任总裁罗伯特·伊索姆 (Robert Isom) 在接受 CNBC 采访时总结了这一商业逻辑：“基本经济舱不是降价。”该票价创造了较低的价格点，但也允许航空公司对标准产品收取更高的费用。航空公司没有对现有经济舱机票打折，而是取消了部分优惠，并将这些优惠置于更高的票价后面。
基础经济也决定了价格比较。较低的广告票价会在搜索结果中引起注意；然后，预订页面会显示其局限性以及避免这些局限性的成本。一旦后果变得清晰，购物者可能会认为差异是可以接受的。即使航空公司希望顾客全买，入门价格也已经发挥了作用。
购买率比基础经济舱销量更重要
航空公司可以通过有多少乘客转向更高的票价来判断基本经济舱的成功，而不仅仅是通过购买最便宜机票的数量来判断。美国航空表示，大约 60% 的选择基本经济舱选项的乘客付费升级为标准经济舱。联合航空公司的这一比例更高，该公司的限制历来是业内最严格的。美联航高管此前表示，只有 16% 的国内乘客实际购买了基本经济舱。
这些数字解释了为什么航空公司保留他们不一定希望大多数客户购买的票价。基础经济舱作为参考价格，而标准经济舱则适用于那些认为节省的费用不足以证明限制合理的旅客。低廉的票价也仍然可以吸引那些可能会选择竞争对手的购物者。预订界面可以立即进行比较：忽略的优惠会与下一层的价格一起显示。乘客会权衡具体的不便与避免这些不便的成本。例如，担心坐在一起的家庭可能会将更高的票价视为实际需要，而不是可选的升级。

乘客可以有效地进行自我分类：那些接受中间座位和严格条件的人选择较低的票价，而那些重视可预测性的人则支付更高的费用。因此，几乎相同的座位可以产生不同的收入。这些数字不应被视为两家航空公司当前的同类转化率。它们来自不同的披露和时期，美联航 16% 的数字描述的是购买基本经济舱的国内旅客的比例，而不是升舱的购物者的比例。尽管如此，这一对比还是说明了为什么承运商可以销售相对较少的基本机票，同时受益于票价显示中的产品。最便宜的选择有助于确定市场的进入价格；更重要的商业成果是通过各种票价选择赚取的收入。
基础经济与标准经济之间的资金差距大幅拉大。 Thrifty Traveler 2026 年 10 月的评论发现，阿拉斯加航空、美国航空、达美航空、捷蓝航空和联合航空的国内航班标准经济舱往返费用通常至少高出 100 美元。有些比较接近或超过 150 美元，尤其是达美航空。额外费用不再局限于长途旅行或出行高峰期；它可以出现在相对较短的国内航线上。

在跨大西洋航线上，差价已从几年前的大约 150 美元往返上升到如今的大约 240 美元。有些航线的费用更高，例如从洛杉矶飞往东京的航线，达美航空的标准经济舱价格比主要基本航线高出数百美元。这些是票价比较，而不是固定费用。随着收入管理系统调整价格，这一差距会随着路线、日期、需求和剩余库存的变化而变化。一个行程 100 美元的差额并不是普遍的附加费，但更广泛的模式表明，恢复标准经济福利已经变得更加昂贵。
航空公司正在取消忠诚度福利以使升舱更具吸引力

现在的限制已经超出了航班本身的范围。航空公司减少了最低票价的奖励，使得基本经济舱对于飞行常客和地位追求者来说变得不那么有价值。美联航更改了 2026 年 4 月 2 日或之后签发的基本经济舱机票的前程万里 (MileagePlus) 赚取方式。没有贵宾 (Premier) 身份或符合条件的美联航信用卡的普通会员不再通过这些票价赚取可兑换里程，而符合条件的精英会员和持卡人仍可赚取减少的里程。这一变化是更广泛的忠诚度改革的一部分，该改革为持有美联航联名卡的客户提供更优惠的赚取率和奖励航班福利。路透社称此举是为了鼓励信用卡的采用并加深对航空公司的忠诚度。路透社和 The Points Guy 概述了这些变化。

title_en: How Many Crew Members Does It Take To Fly A V-22 Osprey?
title_zh: 驾驶 V-22 鱼鹰需要多少名机组人员？
summary: How many crew members does the V-22 Osprey need? The answer depends on the military service, the mission and the demands of each variant.
summary_zh: V-22 鱼鹰需要多少名机组人员？答案取决于兵役、任务和每种型号的需求。
body_en: How Many Crew Members Does It Take To Fly A V-22 Osprey?

Passionate about promoting aviation, the beauty of flight and the science behind it, Antonio is an avid reader of aviation magazines and books, and he loves visiting airshows all over the world, taking photos and writing about airplanes and helicopters as well. He is currently based in Palermo, Sicily.

The Bell Boeing V-22 Osprey was designed to combine capabilities that conventional helicopters and airplanes cannot offer in quite the same way. But operating such an unusual aircraft involves more than mastering its distinctive flight characteristics. The way military crews work around it can be just as revealing as the machine itself.

The US Marines Corps, United States Air Force and US Navy all operate the Osprey, and Japan has joined them. Yet the aircraft does not occupy quite the same place in each service. Looking at the people responsible for flying it gives a different perspective on the demands of a machine that has never fitted neatly into a single category.

Across the V-22 family, the two pilots are the constant; the rest of the crew depends on the mission. According to the Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) specifications for the MV-22B , the Marine Corps version carries two pilots and one crew chief, a crew of three. The Air Force goes further. As reported by Air Force Special Operations Command , its CV-22 flies with four: a pilot , a copilot and two flight engineers. The Navy matches that number, since NAVAIR's CMV-22B page lists a pilot, a copilot, and two crew chiefs.

The crew difference becomes easier to understand when you consider what the Osprey was designed to do. The Osprey is a tiltrotor, an aircraft that lifts off like a helicopter and then swings its two 38-foot (11.6-meter) proprotors forward to cruise like a turboprop airplane, as the Navy's V-22 fact file explains. The MV-22B was built as the Marines' medium-lift assault aircraft, and NAVAIR says it offers twice the speed, six times the range and three times the payload of the Boeing CH-46E Sea Knight it replaced. Hauling a rifle squad needs two pilots and one person watching the cabin.

Real flights can look different, though: an Osprey pilot writing in Stars and Stripes in November 2024 described flying alongside a copilot and multiple crew chiefs, a hint that the published number is a baseline, not a ceiling.

That baseline works for Marines, who mostly move troops and cargo between ships and shore. It does not work for everyone. If three people can move a platoon across an ocean, what exactly is the fourth person doing on an Air Force Osprey?
Why The Air Force CV-22 Osprey Needs Four Crew Members

The answer begins with the mission. AFSOC describes the CV-22 as an aircraft for long-range infiltration, exfiltration and resupply of special operations forces. It carries integrated threat countermeasures, terrain-following radar and a forward-looking infrared sensor, equipment that a standard assault transport does not need. The fact sheet does not divide the workload, but that sensor suite goes a long way toward explaining why a second specialist sits behind the pilots. The Air Force's current CV-22B fact sheet uses the title special mission aviator, while older sheets say flight engineer.

The performance figures show how demanding the job is. The AFSOC lists a maximum speed of 280 knots (519 km/h), a ceiling of 25,000 feet (7,620 meters), and a combat radius of 500 nautical miles (926 km) with one internal auxiliary fuel tank . The cabin holds 24 seated personnel or 10,000 lb (4,536 kg) of cargo, and a .50-caliber machine gun covers the ramp. According to our previous report, the CV-22B is based at Cannon Air Force Base (CVS) in New Mexico, alongside the Lockheed Martin MC-130J Commando II and the A C-130 J Ghostrider gunship.

The Navy's version carries the same four-person crew, but for a very different reason. Rather than inserting special operations teams, the CMV-22B moves people and priority cargo to aircraft carriers at sea. That raises a practical question: what does the second crew chief contribute to a delivery flight?

The CMV-22B replaces the Grumman C-2A Greyhound on the carrier onboard delivery mission, hauling personnel, mail and priority cargo from shore bases to ships at sea. NAVAIR says the Navy version adds extended range, a beyond-line-of-sight HF radio, a passenger public address system and improved cargo lighting, and that it can move up to 6,000 lb (2,722 kg) of cargo or people over 1,150 nautical miles (1,323 miles, or 2,130 km). Every extra feature is another system a crew member has to monitor, and the Navy's passengers are often sailors who have never ridden in a tiltrotor and need briefing, seating, and a calm voice during every conversion.

The Navy's own history shows how the crew took shape. On July 12, 2018, USNI News reported that an all-Navy crew flew an Osprey for the first time, two pilots and two aircrewmen, from Naval Station Norfolk to Marine Corps Air Station New River. Passengers, pallets, and a moving flight deck leave little room for a one-person cabin, and a second crew chief gives the pilots another set of eyes on the ramp, the cargo, and the deck crew during every approach. Simple Flying's coverage of the Greyhound's replacement adds that the Osprey's vertical capability lets it land on decks that helicopters such as the Sikorsky SH-60 Seahawk already use, in most cases. The cabin crew can keep passengers, cargo and the ramp under control, but they do not take the pilots' place.

A second crew chief gives the Navy more help in the cabin, particularly when cargo, passengers and carrier operations compete for attention. But that still leaves the most unusual part of the job unexplained. The Osprey must change from helicopter to airplane mode in flight, and the people managing that transition cannot afford to lose track of what is happening around them.
Emergency squawks, holds, NOTAMs — live signals, no signup.
How V-22 Osprey Pilots Manage Tiltrotor Flights

The Osprey's transition between helicopter and airplane flight is central to the pilots' workload. The Navy fact file says the Osprey has triple-redundant fly-by-wire flight controls designed to reduce pilot workload, which matters because the pilots must also tilt the nacelles, the engine and proprotor assemblies on each wingtip, between helicopter and airplane modes. Moving from vertical flight to forward flight is the Osprey's defining task, and doing it safely, with two sets of hands on the controls and one set of eyes in the cabin, is a team sport. The Stars and Stripes pilot credited three things for making that manageable: a progressive training pipeline, cockpit technology that sharpens situational awareness, and a crew large enough that no one flies alone.
body_zh: 驾驶 V-22 鱼鹰需要多少名机组人员？
安东尼奥热衷于推广航空、飞行之美及其背后的科学，是航空杂志和书籍的狂热读者，他喜欢参观世界各地的航展，也喜欢拍摄有关飞机和直升机的照片和撰写有关飞机和直升机的文章。他目前居住在西西里岛巴勒莫。
贝尔波音 V-22 鱼鹰的设计结合了传统直升机和飞机无法以完全相同的方式提供的功能。但操作如此不寻常的飞机不仅仅需要掌握其独特的飞行特性。军事人员围绕它工作的方式就像机器本身一样具有启发性。
美国海军陆战队、美国空军和美国海军都拥有鱼鹰，日本也加入其中。然而，飞机在每项服务中占据的位置并不完全相同。看看负责飞行的人员，我们可以从不同的角度来看待一台从未完全归入单一类别的机器的需求。

在 V-22 系列中，两名飞行员是不变的。其余的船员取决于任务。根据海军航空系统司令部（NAVAIR）对 MV-22B 的规格，海军陆战队版本可搭载两名飞行员和一名机组长，机组人员为三人。空军走得更远。据空军特种作战司令部报道，其 CV-22 共有 4 名飞行员：一名飞行员、一名副驾驶和两名飞行工程师。海军与这个数字相符，因为 NAVAIR 的 CMV-22B 页面列出了一名飞行员、一名副驾驶和两名机组长。

当您考虑“鱼鹰”的设计用途时，船员之间的差异就更容易理解了。正如海军 V-22 事实文件所解释的那样，“鱼鹰”是一种倾转旋翼机，它像直升机一样升空，然后向前摆动两个 38 英尺（11.6 米）长的螺旋桨，像涡轮螺旋桨飞机一样巡航。 MV-22B 是作为海军陆战队的中型攻击机而制造的，NAVAIR 表示，它的速度是其所取代的波音 CH-46E 海骑士的两倍，航程是六倍，有效载荷是三倍。牵引一支步枪小队需要两名飞行员和一名看守机舱的人。
不过，真实的飞行可能看起来有所不同：2024 年 11 月，一名鱼鹰飞行员在《星条旗报》上撰文描述了与副驾驶和多名机组长并肩飞行的情况，这暗示公布的数字是基线，而不是上限。
该基线适用于海军陆战队，他们主要在舰船和海岸之间运送部队和货物。它并不适合所有人。如果三个人可以带领一个排穿越海洋，那么空军鱼鹰上的第四个人到底在做什么呢？
为什么空军 CV-22 鱼鹰需要四名机组人员
答案始于使命。 AFSOC 将 CV-22 描述为一种用于特种作战部队远程渗透、渗透和补给的飞机。它携带综合威胁对策、地形跟踪雷达和前视红外传感器，这些设备是标准突击运输机不需要的。情况说明书没有划分工作量，但传感器套件在很大程度上解释了为什么第二位专家坐在飞行员后面。空军当前的 CV-22B 情况说明书使用“特殊任务飞行员”这一头衔，而较旧的说明书则称“飞行工程师”。

绩效数据显示了这项工作的要求有多么高。 AFSOC 列出的最大速度为 280 节（519 公里/小时），升限为 25,000 英尺（7,620 米），在配备 1 个内部辅助油箱的情况下，作战半径为 500 海里（926 公里）。机舱可容纳 24 名人员或 10,000 磅（4,536 公斤）的货物，舷梯上覆盖着一挺 0.50 口径机枪。根据我们之前的报道，CV-22B 与洛克希德·马丁公司 MC-130J Commando II 和 A C-130 J Ghostrider 武装直升机一起驻扎在新墨西哥州的坎农空军基地 (CVS)。
海军版本配备了相同的四人机组人员，但出于截然不同的原因。 CMV-22B 不是派遣特种作战小组，而是将人员和优先货物转移到海上的航空母舰上。这就提出了一个实际问题：第二位机组长对运送航班有何贡献？

CMV-22B 取代格鲁门 C-2A 灰狗执行航母舰上投递任务，将人员、邮件和优先货物从岸上基地运送到海上船只。 NAVAIR 表示，海军版本增加了航程、超视距高频无线电、乘客公共广播系统和改进的货物照明，并且可以将重达 6,000 磅（2,722 公斤）的货物或人员移动超过 1,150 海里（1,323 英里或 2,130 公里）。每一个额外的功能都是机组人员必须监控的另一个系统，海军的乘客通常是从未乘坐过倾转旋翼机的水手，在每次转换过程中都需要简报、座位和平静的声音。

海军自身的历史展示了船员是如何形成的。 2018 年 7 月 12 日，美国海军学院新闻报道称，全海军机组人员首次驾驶鱼鹰（包括两名飞行员和两名机组人员）从诺福克海军基地飞往新河海军陆战队航空站。乘客、托盘和移动的飞行甲板几乎没有留给单人舱的空间，而第二名机组长在每次进近时都会让飞行员另一双眼睛注视着坡道、货物和甲板机组人员。 Simple Flying 对灰狗替代品的报道补充道，鱼鹰的垂直能力使其能够降落在西科斯基 SH-60 海鹰等直升机在大多数情况下已经使用的甲板上。机组人员可以控制乘客、货物和坡道，但他们不能代替飞行员。
第二名机组长在机舱内为海军提供更多帮助，特别是当货物、乘客和航母操作争夺注意力时。但这仍然无法解释这项工作中最不寻常的部分。鱼鹰必须在飞行中从直升机模式转变为飞机模式，而管理这种转变的人员不能忽视周围发生的事情。

V-22 鱼鹰飞行员如何管理倾转旋翼机飞行

summary: Southwest's Boeing 737 MAX 7 will debut in March 2027 with 150 seats, Starlink Wi-Fi and 13 more seats than the airline's 737-700s.

Southwest Airlines is preparing to introduce the Boeing 737 MAX 7 into passenger service in March 2027, marking a significant milestone in the carrier's fleet modernization strategy. According to an internal rollout document obtained by View From The Wing , the first aircraft are expected to arrive later this year and feature new seats, WiFi, in-seat power, and larger overhead bins. The new aircraft will offer 13 more seats than Southwest's 737-700s, helping the airline modernize its fleet while increasing capacity on existing routes.

The introduction comes after years of certification delays for Boeing's smallest MAX variant. Southwest has accumulated a substantial number of 737 MAX 7 orders, with the aircraft expected to replace older narrowbodies and support selected route expansions. Beyond the additional seating capacity, the aircraft will also introduce several cabin improvements designed to modernize Southwest's onboard experience.
Southwest's 737 MAX 7 Set To Enter Service In March 2027

Southwest's first 737 MAX 7s are expected to begin passenger operations in March 2027, following deliveries starting in December 2026. According to View From The Wing, the airline will initially operate 27 already-built aircraft, with newly manufactured examples expected to arrive from February 2027. Before entering commercial service, each aircraft will undergo configuration work, maintenance, and validation flights.

The planned introduction follows a major regulatory breakthrough for Boeing: the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) recently granted the 737 MAX 7 type certification on August 3 . The approval came after an extensive certification process involving flight testing, ground testing, safety assessments, and design reviews. It cleared the way for Boeing to begin delivering the aircraft, with Southwest, the variant's launch customer, preparing to receive its first examples. The milestone also removes one of the most significant obstacles that had kept the smallest member of the MAX family out of commercial service for years.

The new aircraft will feature 150 Recaro seats, including designated extra-legroom seating, alongside Starlink connectivity, in-seat power and larger overhead bins. The cabin will also have three lavatories, up from two on Southwest's existing 737-700s. Interestingly, the airline's earlier 2024 investor presentation indicated a 148-seat configuration, meaning the final layout accommodates two additional passengers. The March 2027 introduction remains subject to change as Southwest completes its operational preparations.
Why The 737 MAX 7 Is So Important To Southwest's Fleet Strategy

Introducing the MAX 7 is an important step because Southwest operates a substantial fleet of older 737-700s . Many of these aircraft have been in service for about two decades, making fleet renewal a key consideration for the airline. Replacing them with the newer generation will allow Southwest to modernize its narrowbody fleet while increasing passenger capacity without moving to a substantially larger aircraft.

The MAX 7 will also support Southwest's Hawaiian operations. The first 27 examples can gradually take over extended overwater missions currently performed by older 737-800s . Routes such as Burbank–Honolulu, Phoenix–Hawaii and Las Vegas–Hawaii are among the operations that could benefit from the aircraft's capabilities. Southwest could then reassign the existing 737-800s to other routes, giving it more flexibility across its domestic network.

Southwest's preparation schedule includes multiple flights for each prebuilt aircraft after its initial configuration work, including a simulated extended overwater operation lasting more than 3.5 hours. The airline also plans additional flights across the fleet to ensure the aircraft are ready before commercial operations begin. According to the reported document, Southwest intends to include the MAX 7 in its published schedules before the end of 2026.
MAX 7 Vs. -700: 13 More Seats And A More Efficient Successor

The 737 MAX 7 is slightly longer than the 737-700, despite occupying a similar position within the manufacturer's narrowbody family. Its updated design, more efficient engines, and increased capacity make it a natural successor to Southwest's smaller Next Generation aircraft.

The additional 13 seats represent approximately 9.5% more passenger capacity per aircraft. However, Southwest has deliberately stopped at 150 seats because US regulations generally require an additional flight attendant for aircraft configured with 151 or more passenger seats . This allows the airline to increase capacity without adding another cabin crew member solely because of the seating arrangement.

Southwest has substantial growth potential, with many undelivered 737 MAX 7s and MAX 8s in its order book. The MAX 7 will play an important role in both fleet replacement and network development as the airline transitions toward a more modern narrowbody fleet. Its combination of additional seating, improved cabin amenities, and operational flexibility could make it one of the most important aircraft in Southwest's future fleet strategy.
body_zh: 西南航空的波音 737 MAX 7 将于 2027 年 3 月首次亮相，座位数比 -700 多 13 个
经验丰富的国际民航组织飞行员和空中交通管制员英语语言能力讲师以及会议口译员，热衷于促进航空相关业务中的有效沟通。对航空业有深入的了解，包括航空法规、术语和行业特定的通信协议。自 2014 年以来，她一直在欧洲各地的众多航展上工作。作为一名超轻型飞行员，她在业余时间还致力于提高航空运营的安全性和效率。

西南航空正准备于 2027 年 3 月将波音 737 MAX 7 投入客运服务，这标志着该航空公司机队现代化战略的一个重要里程碑。根据 View From The Wing 获得的一份内部部署文件，第一架飞机预计将于今年晚些时候抵达，并配备新座椅、WiFi、座椅内电源和更大的头顶行李箱。新飞机将比西南航空的 737-700 多提供 13 个座位，帮助该航空公司实现机队现代化，同时增加现有航线的运力。
此次推出是在波音最小的 MAX 型号的认证延迟多年之后推出的。西南航空已积累了大量 737 MAX 7 订单，预计该飞机将取代旧型窄体飞机并支持选定的航线扩张。除了增加座位数外，该飞机还将引入多项客舱改进，旨在使西南航空的机上体验现代化。
西南航空 737 MAX 7 将于 2027 年 3 月投入运营
西南航空的首批 737 MAX 7 预计将于 2026 年 12 月开始交付，并于 2027 年 3 月开始客运运营。据 View From The Wing 称，该航空公司最初将运营 27 架已制造的飞机，新制造的飞机预计将于 2027 年 2 月抵达。在进入商业服务之前，每架飞机都将进行配置工作、维护和验证飞行。

此次计划的推出是在波音取得重大监管突破之后进行的：美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 最近于 8 月 3 日授予了 737 MAX 7 型号认证。此次批准是在经过了广泛的认证过程后获得的，其中包括飞行测试、地面测试、安全评估和设计审查。它为波音公司开始交付这款飞机扫清了道路，该型号的启动客户西南航空正准备接收第一架飞机。这一里程碑还消除了多年来使 MAX 系列最小成员无法投入商业服务的最重大障碍之一。

新飞机将配备 150 个 Recaro 座椅，包括指定的额外腿部空间座椅、Starlink 连接、座椅内电源和更大的头顶行李箱。客舱内还将设有三个卫生间，而西南航空现有 737-700 飞机上只有两个。有趣的是，该航空公司在 2024 年早些时候的投资者演示中指出了 148 个座位的配置，这意味着最终布局可容纳另外两名乘客。随着西南航空完成运营准备工作，2027 年 3 月的推出仍有可能发生变化。
为什么 737 MAX 7 对西南航空的机队战略如此重要
引进 MAX 7 是重要的一步，因为西南航空拥有大量老式 737-700 机队。其中许多飞机已经服役了大约二十年，因此机队更新成为该航空公司的一个关键考虑因素。用新一代飞机取代它们将使西南航空能够对其窄体机机队进行现代化改造，同时增加载客量，而无需转向更大的飞机。
MAX 7 还将支持西南航空的夏威夷业务。前 27 架飞机可以逐渐接管目前由老式 737-800 飞机执行的长期水上任务。伯班克-檀香山、菲尼克斯-夏威夷和拉斯维加斯-夏威夷等航线都可以受益于该飞机的功能。然后，西南航空可以将现有的 737-800 飞机重新分配给其他航线，从而在其国内网络中提供更大的灵活性。
西南航空的准备计划包括每架预制飞机在初始配置工作后进行多次飞行，其中包括持续超过 3.5 小时的模拟扩展水上操作。该航空公司还计划在机队中增加航班，以确保飞机在商业运营开始之前做好准备。据报道，西南航空打算在 2026 年底前将 MAX 7 纳入其公布的航班时刻表中。
最多 7 VS。 -700：增加 13 个席位和更高效的继任者
737 MAX 7 比 737-700 稍长，尽管它们在制造商的窄体飞机系列中占据相似的位置。其更新的设计、更高效的发动机和增加的容量使其成为西南航空较小的下一代飞机的自然继承者。
新增 13 个座位意味着每架飞机的载客量增加约 9.5%。不过，西南航空特意将座位数停在了150个，因为美国法规通常要求配置151个或更多乘客座位的飞机配备额外的空乘人员。这使得航空公司能够增加运力，而无需仅仅因为座位安排而增加另一名机组人员。
西南航空拥有巨大的增长潜力，其订单中有许多未交付的 737 MAX 7 和 MAX 8。随着航空公司向更现代化的窄体机队转型，MAX 7 将在机队更换和网络发展方面发挥重要作用。其额外座位、改进的机舱设施和操作灵活性的结合可能使其成为西南航空未来机队战略中最重要的飞机之一。

title_en: Hawaiian Airlines Is Overhauling The Premium Experience On 24 Airbus A330s, But Isn't Even Touching Its Narrowbodies
title_zh: 夏威夷航空正在彻底改革 24 架空客 A330 的高级体验，但甚至没有触及其窄体飞机
summary: With its narrowbody aircraft retiring or their futures in doubt, Hawaiian is currently concentrating on replacing only widebody interiors.
summary_zh: 由于窄体飞机退役或前景不明，夏威夷航空目前专注于仅更换宽体飞机内饰。
body_en: Hawaiian Airlines Is Overhauling The Premium Experience On 24 Airbus A330s, But Isn't Even Touching Its Narrowbodies

Aaron is an aviation enthusiast and world traveler with a deep interest in aerospace history and technology. He has traveled around the world numerous times, often incorporating visits to aviation museums and historic aircraft collections into his journeys. A native of New Zealand, he is an expert in aviation and maintains a broad interest in a variety of other subjects.

Alaska Airlines has completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Airlines and is in the process of modernizing and changing its fleet. Modernization is somewhat nuanced, as the takeover has deprived Hawaiian of its planned Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner fleet without direct replacement. For now, Alaska is concentrating on upgrading the interiors of Hawaiian's fleet of 24 Airbus A330-200 airliners and retiring its aging fleet of Boeing 717 regional airliners.

At the same time, Alaska is mulling the future of Hawaiian Airlines' most modern fleet, the A321neo. Alaska's CFO has previously said Hawaiian's A321neo fleet will either double in size or be phased out entirely , so investing in new interiors would be risky until that's decided. This means that Hawaiian's A321neos are in limbo while the A330 fleet is cleared to receive a mid-life cabin upgrade.

In September 2026, Hawaiian Airlines announced it was overhauling its interisland fleet and A330 cabins. At the time, Hawaii's parent company, Alaska Air, hosted an Investor Day in Seattle unveiling new lie-flat suites for both its brands: Aurora and Leihoku. The statement said Hawaiian will reconfigure its A330s with new interiors and four cabin types by 2028.

Hawaiian Airlines CEO Diana Birkett Rakow explained, " The front cabin will be the Leihoku Suites, full lie flat seats with a door closed suite. The second cabin is something called premium reserve, so think of that as like domestic business class with a little bit larger seats, larger pitch, a different level of service, and then there’s premium economy and main cabin ." The retrofit will remove four economy (main cabin) seats and replace them with 12 high-class seats.

The airline said the changes won't directly lower interisland prices, but they will indirectly help by letting the airline earn more from high-class passengers. Rakow explained, " When you have more revenue coming from the front of the airplane, that takes the pressure off the back of the airplane ." The airline also said it will retire its older Boeing 717 aircraft as these aircraft are becoming increasingly expensive to operate , partly because there are more fuel-efficient alternatives.

Hawaiian currently operates a fleet of 71 aircraft, or 61 if the 11 cargo A330-300P2F freighters are excluded. The widebody passenger fleet is composed of 24 Airbus A330-200s. These are currently configured with 18 business class seats and 260 economy class seats, of which 68 are classified as 'Premium Class.' These will be retrofitted with 22 business class seats, 28 premium economy seats, and 204 economy class seats, of which 48 will be 'Premium Class.'

The A330s are now an average of 13.4 years old, meaning they are approaching midlife. The 19-strong fleet of 717s is to be replaced with mid-aged 737-800 aircraft, which are to be transferred from Alaska starting in 2028. Hawaiian has currently received one 737-800 from Alaska. The airline also operates a fleet of 18 A321neo aircraft, the most modern and fuel-efficient in the fleet. The Boeing 717s serve interisland routes, while the A321neos have the range to reach farther destinations.

Hawaiian was originally a customer for Airbus' shorter A350-800 variant , which was never built, as Airbus instead elected to upgrade the A330ceo to the A330neo. The airline then switched its order to the A330-800neo variant of the A330neo family, but, seeing the type was extremely unpopular, it dropped the order and selected to purchase 12 787-9s. As Alaska acquired Hawaiian, it took over the order for 787-9s to develop its own long-haul network. Hawaiian is therefore left with its existing A330-300 widebody fleet.
Hawaiian Is Set To Retire Its Boeing 717 Fleet

Hawaiian is leaving its 717 regional aircraft out of the planned cabin upgrades as they are due to be retired and replaced in the next few years. Hawaiian Airlines and Delta Air Lines are the last two commercial passenger airlines operating the 717 after QantasLink retired its fleet. The Boeing 717 was developed for the 100-seat regional market and was originally marketed by McDonnell Douglas in the early 1990s as the McDonnell Douglas MD-95.

It shares a common lineage with the MD-80 and the broader Douglas DC-9 family. However, the type is aging, and its fuel efficiency is becoming a growing problem, especially during periods of high fuel prices. Delta is the larger operator of the two, and it is accelerating the retirement of its Boeing 717 fleet and pulling select jets from service ahead of a full scheduled phaseout.

Beyond high fuel costs, the type is increasingly suffering from high maintenance costs from heavy maintenance checks, structural inspections, and corrosion remediation, as well as issues maintaining its Rolls-Royce BR715 engines. While Delta is partly replacing its fleet with modern Airbus A220s, Hawaiian will get older 737-800s, which are an improvement but still previous-generation aircraft. It is unclear when Hawaiian's 717 fleet will fully retire, but the phase-out is set to begin in 2028.
The Uncertainty Around Hawaiian's A321neo Fleet

Alaska Airlines operates an all-Boeing fleet; until taking delivery of the 787s , it was an all-737 mainline fleet, excluding Embraer commuter aircraft. Its acquisition of Hawaiian has thrown the future of the A321neos into question, even though they are the airline's most modern aircraft with an average age of just seven years. Currently, Alaska has not said it would divest of them, but it also hasn't committed to retaining them.

The A321neos were originally a very important part of Hawaiian's strategy to serve thinner mainland-Hawaii routes, mostly from the West Coast. They also offer considerably better economics than its existing A330 fleet on thinner routes. Alaska Air Group has around 168 firm 737 MAX orders (deliveries through 2035) and options for another 71. Alaskan executives have previously said that Hawaiian's fleet of 18 A321neos is probably too small to justify maintaining and operating as a permanent subfleet.

Currently, Alaska is considering either retiring them or significantly expanding the fleet. No final decision is expected yet, and the aircraft will remain in a holding pattern until around 2027-2028. With this uncertainty, there is little sense in Hawaiian retrofitting the cabins as it is with the A330 fleet.

body_zh: 夏威夷航空正在彻底改革 24 架空客 A330 的高级体验，但甚至没有触及其窄体飞机
亚伦是一位航空爱好者和环球旅行家，对航空航天历史和技术有着浓厚的兴趣。他曾多次环游世界，经常在旅途中参观航空博物馆和历史飞机收藏。他是新西兰人，是航空专家，并对其他各种学科保持着广泛的兴趣。
阿拉斯加航空已完成对夏威夷航空的收购，并正在进行机队现代化和改造。现代化建设有些微妙，因为此次收购剥夺了夏威夷航空计划中的波音 787-9 梦想客机机队，且无法直接更换。目前，阿拉斯加航空正集中精力升级夏威夷航空 24 架空客 A330-200 客机机队的内饰，并退役其老化的波音 717 支线客机机队。
与此同时，阿拉斯加正在考虑夏威夷航空最现代化机队 A321neo 的未来。阿拉斯加航空公司的首席财务官此前曾表示，夏威夷航空的 A321neo 机队规模要么会扩大一倍，要么会完全淘汰，因此在做出决定之前投资新的内饰将是有风险的。这意味着夏威夷航空的 A321neo 陷入困境，而 A330 机队则已获准进行中年客舱升级。
2026 年 9 月，夏威夷航空宣布对其岛际机队和 A330 客舱进行大修。当时，夏威夷航空的母公司阿拉斯加航空在西雅图举办了投资者日活动，推出了其两个品牌 Aurora 和 Leihoku 的全新平躺套房。声明称，夏威夷航空将在 2028 年之前重新配置其 A330 飞机，配备新的内饰和四种客舱类型。
夏威夷航空首席执行官 Diana Birkett Rakow 解释说：“前舱将是 Leihoku 套房，全平躺式座椅，门关闭套房。第二个舱是所谓的高级预留舱，因此可以将其想象为国内商务舱，座位稍大一些，间距更大，服务水平不同，然后还有高级经济舱和主舱。”此次改装将取消4个经济舱（主舱）座椅，并更换为12个高级座椅。
该航空公司表示，这些变化不会直接降低岛际价格，但会通过让航空公司从高级乘客身上赚取更多收入来间接提供帮助。拉科夫解释说：“当飞机前部获得更多收入时，飞机后部的压力就会减轻。”该航空公司还表示，将退役较旧的波音 717 飞机，因为这些飞机的运营成本越来越高，部分原因是有更省油的替代品。
夏威夷航空目前运营着一支由 71 架飞机组成的机队，如果不包括 11 架 A330-300P2F 货机，则为 61 架飞机。宽体客机机队由 24 架空客 A330-200 组成。目前配置有 18 个商务舱座位和 260 个经济舱座位，其中 68 个座位被归类为“高级舱”。这些座位将改装为 22 个商务舱座位、28 个豪华经济舱座位和 204 个经济舱座位，其中 48 个为“豪华舱”座位。
目前，A330 的平均机龄为 13.4 年，这意味着它们已接近中年。 19 架 717 机队将从 2028 年开始从阿拉斯加转移到中年 737-800 飞机来取代。夏威夷航空目前已从阿拉斯加接收了一架 737-800 飞机。该航空公司还运营着一支由 18 架 A321neo 飞机组成的机队，是机队中最现代化、最节能的飞机。波音 717 提供岛际航线，而 A321neo 则可飞往更远的目的地。

夏威夷航空最初是空客较短的 A350-800 型号的客户，但该型号从未制造，因为空客选择将 A330ceo 升级为 A330neo。随后，该航空公司将其订单转为 A330neo 系列的 A330-800neo 变型，但由于该机型极不受欢迎，因此放弃了订单并选择购买 12 787-9。随着阿拉斯加航空收购夏威夷航空，它接手了 787-9 的订单，以开发自己的长途网络。因此，夏威夷航空仅保留其现有的 A330-300 宽体机队。
夏威夷航空即将退役其波音 717 机队
夏威夷航空将其 717 支线飞机排除在客舱升级计划之外，因为这些飞机将在未来几年内退役和更换。夏威夷航空和达美航空是 QantasLink 机队退役后最后两家运营 717 的商业客运航空公司。波音 717 是为 100 座的区域市场开发的，最初由麦道公司于 20 世纪 90 年代初以麦道公司 MD-95 的名称进行销售。
它与 MD-80 和更广泛的道格拉斯 DC-9 系列具有共同的血统。然而，该类型正在老化，其燃油效率正成为一个日益严重的问题，特别是在高燃油价格时期。达美航空是这两家航空公司中规模较大的运营商，该公司正在加速其波音 717 机队的退役，并在全面淘汰之前停止使用部分飞机。
除了高昂的燃油成本之外，该机型还日益面临繁重的维护检查、结构检查和腐蚀修复以及劳斯莱斯 BR715 发动机维护问题带来的高维护成本。虽然达美航空正在用现代空客 A220 飞机部分替换其机队，但夏威夷航空将购买较旧的 737-800 飞机，这是一种改进，但仍然是上一代飞机。目前尚不清楚夏威夷航空的 717 机队何时完全退役，但逐步淘汰将于 2028 年开始。
夏威夷航空 A321neo 机队的不确定性
阿拉斯加航空运营着一支全波音机队；在接收 787 之前，这是一支全部由 737 组成的干线机队，不包括巴西航空工业公司的通勤飞机。它对夏威夷航空的收购让 A321neo 的未来受到质疑，尽管它们是该航空公司最现代化的飞机，平均机龄只有七年。目前，阿拉斯加尚未表示将剥离它们，但也没有承诺保留它们。

A321neo 最初是夏威夷航空战略中非常重要的一部分，旨在服务于较稀疏的大陆至夏威夷航线（主要来自西海岸）。在狭窄航线上，它们还比现有的 A330 机队提供更好的经济性。阿拉斯加航空集团拥有约 168 架 737 MAX 确认订单（交付至 2035 年），以及另外 71 架的选择权。阿拉斯加航空高管此前曾表示，夏威夷航空的 18 架 A321neo 机队可能太小，无法作为永久子机队进行维护和运营。
目前，阿拉斯加正在考虑要么让它们退役，要么大幅扩大机队规模。预计尚未做出最终决定，该飞机将保持搁置状态，直到 2027 年至 2028 年左右。由于存在这种不确定性，夏威夷航空公司像 A330 机队那样改造客舱没有什么意义。

title_en: How To Redeem Alaska Atmos Rewards Points: Rules, Fees, & Sweet Spots
title_zh: 如何兑换阿拉斯加 Atmos 奖励积分：规则、费用和最佳选择
summary: Alaska Atmos Rewards has changed a lot, but it remains a favorite points currency. Here's how to earn points, the redemption rules, and the best sweet spots.
summary_zh: 阿拉斯加 Atmos 奖励发生了很大变化，但它仍然是最受欢迎的积分货币。以下是如何赚取积分、兑换规则和最佳甜点
body_en: Alaska Atmos Rewards (formerly Alaska Mileage Plan) has long been a favorite points currency among miles & points geeks, given the carrier’s unique array of airline partners, generous stopover policy, and attractive redemption rates.
In this post, I’d like to take an in-depth look at how to redeem Atmos Rewards points. How do you earn Atmos Rewards points, what are the rules around redeeming them, and what are the best uses?
There are several different ways to go about earning Alaska Atmos Rewards points, from credit cards, to outright buying points, to transferring them from other cards.
Earn Atmos Rewards points with co-branded credit cards
The Atmos Rewards program has three co-branded credit cards, issued by Bank of America, and they all have excellent welcome bonuses with limited eligibility restrictions

The Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite ® Credit Card ( learn more ) has a $395 annual fee, and there are so many reasons to get this lucrative card , ranging from the fastest pathway to earning status , to Global Companion Awards , to great bonus categories , and much more

The Atmos™ Rewards Ascent Visa Signature® credit card ( learn more ) has a $95 annual fee, and it offers valuable basic perks for travel on Alaska & Hawaiian, including the ability to earn a $99 companion fare
The Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card ( learn more ) has a minimum of a $95 annual fee ($70 for the company and $25 per user), and offers useful benefits for travel on Alaska & Hawaiian

What’s so great is that you can potentially qualify for all of these cards, so that’s an opportunity to earn lots of points. For example, I picked up both the Atmos Rewards Summit Card and Atmos Rewards Business Card on the same day.
Earn Atmos Rewards points with other credit cards

The Atmos Rewards program is transfer partners with Bilt Rewards , so you can transfer Bilt points to Atmos Rewards at a 1:1 ratio. This could be a great reason to pick up one of Bilt’s credit cards , with options including the Bilt Blue Card ( learn more ), Bilt Obsidian Card ( learn more ), and Bilt Palladium Card ( learn more ) ( Rates & Fees ). Personally, I think the Bilt Palladium Card is by far the most lucrative .
You can even pay rent with an Atmos Rewards card and earn 3x points while paying a 3% fee, which could be a useful deal, especially if you’re pursuing elite status.

The program also partners with Marriott Bonvoy, so you can transfer over Marriott points . The ratio is that 60,000 Bonvoy points convert into 25,000 Atmos Rewards points (if you convert in different increments it’s a 3:1 ratio).

This can be a solid value, and there are lots of credit cards that can earn you Bonvoy points, including the Marriott Bonvoy Business® American Express® Card ( learn more ), Marriott Bonvoy Bevy® American Express® Card ( learn more ), and Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant® American Express® Card ( learn more ).

The Atmos Rewards program is pretty aggressive about selling points , and the program seems to offer promotions on purchased points every couple of months. When we see these offers, you can expect bonuses in the range of 90-110%. This is often an opportunity to acquire Atmos Rewards points for under two cents each.

It doesn’t cost anything to join the Atmos Rewards program , so I generally recommend signing up ahead of time — you have to be a member for at least 10 days in order to take advantage of one of these promotions.
Not only are there great ways to earn Atmos Rewards points either through credit cards or by buying them outright, but Atmos Rewards is also a good program to credit flights to.

For one, Atmos Rewards is the last major US frequent flyer program to give members the option to earn points based on distance flown rather than dollars spent. Atmos Rewards allows mileage earning on a variety of airline partners, ranging from Condor to Cathay Pacific. Atmos Rewards lets you earn points for travel on the following airline partners

The one thing worth mentioning is that you can only earn Atmos Rewards points on Korean Air, Philippine Airlines, and Starlux Airlines, if you book through Alaska, rather than through one of the partners.
Basics of redeeming Alaska Atmos Rewards points
body_zh: 阿拉斯加 Atmos 奖励（原阿拉斯加里程计划）长期以来一直是里程和积分爱好者最喜欢的积分货币，因为该航空公司拥有独特的航空公司合作伙伴、慷慨的中途停留政策和有吸引力的兑换率。
在这篇文章中，我想深入了解如何兑换 Atmos Rewards 积分。如何赚取 Atmos Rewards 积分、兑换积分的规则是什么以及最佳用途是什么？
赚取阿拉斯加 Atmos 奖励积分有多种不同的方式，从信用卡、直接购买积分到从其他卡转移积分。
使用联名信用卡赚取 Atmos Rewards 积分
Atmos Rewards 计划拥有三张由美国银行发行的联名信用卡，它们都具有丰厚的欢迎奖金，且资格限制有限
Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® 信用卡（了解更多）年费为 395 美元，获得这张利润丰厚的信用卡的理由有很多，从最快的赚钱途径、到全球伙伴奖、到丰厚的奖金类别等等。
Atmos™ Rewards Ascent Visa Signature® 信用卡（了解更多）年费为 95 美元，为阿拉斯加和夏威夷航空旅行提供宝贵的基本福利，包括能够赚取 99 美元的同伴票价
Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® 商务卡（了解更多）的年费最低为 95 美元（公司 70 美元，每位用户 25 美元），并为阿拉斯加和夏威夷旅行提供实用福利
很棒的是，您有可能有资格获得所有这些卡，因此这是赚取大量积分的机会。例如，我在同一天领取了 Atmos Rewards Summit Card 和 Atmos Rewards Business Card。
使用其他信用卡赚取 Atmos Rewards 积分

Atmos Rewards 计划是 Bilt Rewards 的转让合作伙伴，因此您可以将 Bilt 积分以 1:1 的比例转让给 Atmos Rewards。这可能是选择一张 Bilt 信用卡的重要理由，信用卡选项包括 Bilt Blue Card（了解更多）、Bilt Obsidian Card（了解更多）和 Bilt Palladium Card（了解更多）（费率和费用）。就我个人而言，我认为比尔特钯金卡是迄今为止最赚钱的。
您甚至可以使用 Atmos Rewards 卡支付租金，并在支付 3% 的费用的同时赚取 3 倍积分，这可能是一笔有用的交易，尤其是如果您追求精英身份的话。
该计划还与万豪旅享家合作，因此您可以转移万豪积分。该比率为 60,000 Bonvoy 积分可转换为 25,000 Atmos Rewards 积分（如果您以不同的增量进行转换，则比率为 3:1）。
这可以是一个可靠的价值，有很多信用卡可以为您赚取 Bonvoy 积分，包括 Marriott Bonvoy Business® American Express® 卡（了解更多）、Marriott Bonvoy Bevy® American Express® 卡（了解更多）和 Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant® American Express® 卡（了解更多）。
Atmos 奖励计划在卖点方面相当激进，该计划似乎每隔几个月就会对购买的点进行促销。当我们看到这些优惠时，您可以期待 90-110% 的奖金。这通常是一个以每张不到两美分的价格获得 Atmos Rewards 积分的机会。
加入 Atmos 奖励计划不需要任何费用，因此我通常建议提前注册 - 您必须成为会员至少 10 天才能享受其中一项促销活动。
不仅有通过信用卡或直接购买赚取 Atmos Rewards 积分的好方法，而且 Atmos Rewards 也是一个很好的积分航班计划。
首先，Atmos Rewards 是美国最后一个主要的飞行常客计划，会员可以选择根据飞行距离而不是花费的金额来赚取积分。 Atmos Rewards 允许在各种航空公司合作伙伴（从 Condor 到国泰航空）赚取里程。 Atmos Rewards 可让您通过搭乘以下航空公司合作伙伴的航班赚取积分
值得一提的是，如果您通过阿拉斯加而不是通过合作伙伴之一预订，则只能在大韩航空、菲律宾航空和星宇航空上赚取 Atmos 奖励积分。

title_en: JetBlue's Airbus A321LR Has 24 Mint Suites, But Only Sells 23 Of Them
title_zh: 捷蓝航空的空客 A321LR 拥有 24 间薄荷套房，但仅售出 23 间
summary: Crew rest is an essential part of long-haul operations for every airline.
summary_zh: 机组人员休息是每家航空公司长途运营的重要组成部分。
body_en: JetBlue's Airbus A321LR Has 24 Mint Suites, But Only Sells 23 Of Them

Jack comes to Simple Flying with a lifelong interest in all things aviation. He holds a degree in Aerospace Engineering from Georgia Tech, and is a certified private and remote pilot. Beyond these experiences, Jack previously worked for a corporate flight department where he gained first-hand experience in the world of business aviation. Currently, Jack works in the professional services industry and continues to build his flight hours outside of work.

JetBlue Airways' Airbus A321LR has 24 seats in its Mint business-class cabin, but passengers generally can book only 23 of them on transatlantic flights. Suite 12A, which appears to be an ordinary premium seat on the cabin map, is reserved for a relief pilot to rest during the journey. The seemingly missing seat is not a sales-system error or a decision to withhold a desirable product from customers. It is part of the operational setup that allows JetBlue to fly long-haul routes with an augmented flight crew while meeting fatigue-management requirements.

The arrangement illustrates how aircraft seat maps reflect more than the number of seats physically installed. Airlines must balance cabin revenue against the need to provide rest opportunities for crew members operating flights that exceed what a standard crew can safely cover under applicable duty limits. JetBlue uses a business-class suite for pilot rest and reserves seats in the rear economy cabin for flight attendants. Understanding why those places are blocked also reveals how the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) classifies onboard rest facilities, why some crew seats occasionally appear for sale, and how staffing rules shape the passenger experience.
Why Suite 12A Is Missing From JetBlue’s Available Mint Cabin

JetBlue’s A321LR has 24 Mint seats arranged in a one-one configuration across rows one through 12. The cabin combines individual suites with doors and two larger Mint Studios at the front. On transatlantic flights, however, suite 12A is designated for a relief pilot rather than a paying customer. That leaves 23 Mint seats available for sale even though the aircraft physically contains 24 premium seats.

JetBlue’s A321LR was designed to make thinner transatlantic routes viable with a single-aisle aircraft. Its range and cabin configuration allow the airline to connect New York and Boston with European destinations without deploying a larger widebody jet. But flying across the Atlantic requires a crew rest plan: pilots cannot remain on duty for the entire flight without the legally required opportunity to rest, and an augmented crew allows pilots to rotate between active flight duties and rest periods.

The designated suite is a Class 2 rest facility . It offers a lie-flat sleeping surface within the passenger cabin, separated from the rest of the cabin by a thick curtain that reduces light and some noise. The seat therefore serves a safety-related operational purpose rather than a premium amenity. The Points Guy documented the arrangement when JetBlue introduced its A321LR, noting that suite 12A is reserved for relief pilots on transatlantic flights and that flight attendants use seats in the last row of the economy cabin.

Federal regulations define three classes of rest facility for augmented flightcrew operations under 14 CFR Part 117. Class 1 is a bunk or other surface that permits flat sleeping in a separate space away from both the cockpit and passenger cabin. The area must allow temperature control and light management, and provide isolation from noise and disturbance. It is the most distinct type of rest space.

Class 2, the category relevant to JetBlue’s pilot suite, is a cabin seat that allows a flat or near-flat sleeping position. It must be separated from passengers by at least a curtain that provides darkness and some sound mitigation, and it must be reasonably free from disturbance. Class 3 is less elaborate: a seat in the cabin or flight deck that reclines at least 40 degrees and provides leg and foot support. The federal regulation's definitions set out the precise requirements , while the FAA’s Advisory Circular 117-1 explains how approved facilities are used in augmented flightcrew operations.

These categories are not simply labels for passenger comfort; the rest facilities available to pilots affect the maximum flight duty period permitted under the rules, alongside factors such as the scheduled start time and number of pilots assigned. Better rest facilities can support a longer permitted duty period under the applicable framework, while lower-class facilities can impose tighter limits. Operators must have the appropriate facility classification approved before using it for qualifying operations. The FAA’s system also helps explain why a curtain and a flat seat can matter operationally. The goal is not to create a luxury sleeping environment; it is to provide a defined opportunity for rest under conditions that meet the relevant standard.
Crew Rest Has Safety Requirements Beyond A Blocked Seat

A crew rest area must do more than look private on a seat map. Its design and approval depend on the type of facility, the aircraft, and the applicable regulatory requirements. For Class 1 compartments, relevant design and safety provisions include features such as smoke detection, fire protection, lighting, oxygen equipment, seat-belt indications, and communication with the flight deck. The specific equipment requirements vary with the approved design and governing rules, so they should not be assumed to apply identically to every curtained cabin seat.

The FAA’s Advisory Circular 117-1 also outlines criteria for rest facilities used in augmented flightcrew operations. It explains that airlines operating under Part 117 must obtain FAA approval and qualification for the class of onboard rest facility before using it for those operations. A facility’s status is therefore not determined solely by whether a seat reclines far enough or whether a curtain can be pulled around it. Its configuration must meet the relevant criteria.

For passengers, the practical consequence is that crew rest seats can be treated differently from ordinary seats even when they share the same cabin. A blocked suite may remain unavailable throughout booking because it is needed for the scheduled operation. On aircraft with Class 2 or Class 3 facilities, the rest space may be embedded in the passenger cabin, using a seat and a curtain rather than a dedicated compartment. The arrangement saves cabin volume, but it requires airlines to manage passenger access and protect the intended rest period.
Why United’s 767 Crew Seats Sometimes Appear For Sale
body_zh: 捷蓝航空的空客 A321LR 拥有 24 间薄荷套房，但仅售出 23 间
Jack 带着对航空一切事物的终生兴趣加入了 Simple Flying。他拥有佐治亚理工学院的航空航天工程学位，并且是一名经过认证的私人和远程飞行员。除了这些经验之外，杰克还曾在公司飞行部门工作过，在那里他获得了公务航空领域的第一手经验。目前，杰克在专业服务行业工作，并在工作之外继续增加飞行时间。
捷蓝航空的空客 A321LR 的 Mint 商务舱有 24 个座位，但乘客在跨大西洋航班上通常只能预订其中 23 个座位。 12A套房在客舱地图上看似普通的高级座位，是为救援飞行员在旅途中休息而预留的。看似缺失的座位并不是销售系统的错误，也不是拒绝向顾客提供所需产品的决定。它是运营设置的一部分，使捷蓝航空能够在增加机组人员的情况下执飞长途航线，同时满足疲劳管理要求。

这种安排说明了飞机座位图如何反映的不仅仅是实际安装的座位数量。航空公司必须在客舱收入与为运行航班的机组人员提供休息机会（超出标准机组人员在适用的职责限制下可以安全承担的时间）的需求之间取得平衡。捷蓝航空使用商务舱套间供飞行员休息，并在后部经济舱为空乘人员预留座位。了解这些地方被封锁的原因还可以揭示美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 如何对机上休息设施进行分类、为什么一些机组座位偶尔会出现出售，以及人员配置规则如何影响乘客体验。
为什么捷蓝航空可用的 Mint 客舱中缺少 12A 套房
捷蓝航空的 A321LR 有 24 个 Mint 座位，从第 1 排到第 12 排以一对一的方式排列。机舱内设有带门的独立套房和位于前面的两个较大的 Mint Studio。然而，在跨大西洋航班上，12A 套房是为救援飞行员而非付费乘客指定的。尽管这架飞机实际包含 24 个高级座位，但仍剩下 23 个 Mint 座位可供出售。
捷蓝航空的 A321LR 旨在通过单通道飞机打造更稀疏的跨大西洋航线。其航程和客舱配置使该航空公司能够将纽约和波士顿与欧洲目的地连接起来，而无需部署更大的宽体喷气机。但跨越大西洋的飞行需要机组人员休息计划：如果没有法律规定的休息机会，飞行员就不能在整个飞行过程中一直值班，而增强的机组人员允许飞行员在活跃的飞行任务和休息时间之间轮换。
指定套房为二级休息设施。它在客舱内提供了一个平躺的睡眠表面，通过厚窗帘与客舱的其他部分隔开，可以减少光线和噪音。因此，该座椅的作用是与安全相关的操作目的，而不是高级便利设施。 Points Guy 记录了捷蓝航空推出 A321LR 时的安排，并指出 12A 套房是为跨大西洋航班的救援飞行员保留的，空姐则使用经济舱最后一排的座位。
联邦法规根据 14 CFR 第 117 部分规定了三类用于增强飞行机组操作的休息设施。1 类是允许在远离驾驶舱和客舱的单独空间内平躺睡眠的床位或其他表面。该区域必须允许温度控制和灯光管理，并隔离噪音和干扰。这是最独特的休息空间类型。
2 级是与捷蓝航空飞行员套房相关的类别，是一种允许平坦或接近平坦睡眠位置的机舱座椅。它必须与乘客至少用窗帘隔开，以提供黑暗和一定的声音缓解，并且必须相当不受干扰。 3 级则不太复杂：机舱或飞行甲板上的座椅可倾斜至少 40 度并提供腿部和脚部支撑。联邦法规的定义规定了精确的要求，而 FAA 的第 117-1 号咨询通告则解释了如何在增强机组人员操作中使用经批准的设施。

这些类别不仅仅是乘客舒适度的标签，也是乘客舒适度的标签。飞行员可用的休息设施会影响规则允许的最长飞行执勤期限，此外还有预定的开始时间和分配的飞行员人数等因素。更好的休息设施可以支持适用框架下更长的允许值勤期，而较低级别的设施可以施加更严格的限制。运营商必须先获得适当的设施分类批准，然后才能将其用于合格的运营。美国联邦航空局的系统还有助于解释为什么窗帘和平座椅在操作上很重要。我们的目标不是创造一个豪华的睡眠环境；而是创造一个舒适的睡眠环境。其目的是在符合相关标准的条件下提供明确的休息机会。
机组休息的安全要求超出了封闭座位的要求
机组人员休息区的作用不仅仅是在座位图上看起来私密。其设计和批准取决于设施、飞机的类型和适用的监管要求。对于 1 级舱室，相关设计和安全规定包括烟雾探测、消防、照明、氧气设备、安全带指示以及与驾驶舱通信等功能。具体的设备要求因批准的设计和管理规则而异，因此不应假定它们同样适用于每个带窗帘的客舱座椅。
美国联邦航空局 (FAA) 的第 117-1 号咨询通告还概述了增强机组人员操作中使用的休息设施的标准。它解释说，根据第 117 部分运营的航空公司必须先获得美国联邦航空局 (FAA) 的批准和机上休息设施级别的资格，然后才能将其用于这些运营。因此，设施的状态不仅仅取决于座椅是否倾斜足够远或是否可以拉上窗帘。其配置必须符合相关标准。
对于乘客来说，实际后果是，即使共用同一客舱，机组人员休息座椅也可能会受到与普通座椅不同的待遇。被锁定的套房可能在整个预订过程中一直不可用，因为预定的运营需要它。在配备 2 类或 3 类设施的飞机上，休息空间可能嵌入客舱内，使用座椅和窗帘，而不是专用隔间。这种安排节省了客舱容积，但要求航空公司管理旅客出入并保障预定的休息时间。

title_en: Are Marriott Bonvoy Airline Mileage Transfers Worth It? They Could Be, But…
title_zh: 万豪旅享家航空里程转让值得吗？他们可能是，但是……
summary: Marriott Bonvoy points convert into airline miles at a 3:1 ratio, with bonuses on larger transfers. Here's how it works, which partners you can use, and whether it's worth it.
summary_zh: 万豪旅享家积分按 3:1 的比例转换为航空里程，大额转账还可获得奖励。以下是它的工作原理、您可以使用哪些合作伙伴、
body_en: Among hotel loyalty programs , one thing that makes Marriott Bonvoy unique is the ability to (fairly) efficiently convert hotel points into airline miles. While most major hotel loyalty programs allow some sort of opportunity to convert hotel points into airline miles, it typically represents a very bad value.

In this post, I’d like to take a look at the opportunity to convert Marriott points into airline miles. Which airline programs can you move your Marriott points to, what’s the transfer ratio, and is it worth it?
Basics of Marriott’s points to miles transfer option

It’s possible to convert Bonvoy points into airline miles , with your choice of nearly 40 different frequent flyer programs. Let’s take a look at which partners Marriott Bonvoy has, what the transfer ratios are, etc.
Marriott Bonvoy airline miles transfer ratios & bonuses
Marriott points generally convert into airline miles at a 3:1 ratio, and with most partners you get 5,000 bonus miles for every 60,000 Marriott points you transfer.

In other words, 60,000 Bonvoy points will convert into 25,000 airline miles (including the 5,000 bonus miles). You can take advantage of that bonus of 5,000 miles multiple times, meaning that you can convert Bonvoy points into airline miles at a ratio of up to 2.4:1.

Note that you can transfer a minimum of 3,000 Bonvoy points and a maximum of 240,000 Bonvoy points per day. So if you want to transfer more than 240,000 Bonvoy points, you’ll want to do so over multiple days.
Marriott Bonvoy airline mileage transfer partners

Below is a chart with the airline frequent flyer programs you can transfer your Marriott points to, along with the standard transfer ratio, plus the ability to earn a bonus when transferring a minimum of 60,000 points.
